title: Map artifact names to REST endpoints via the endpoint pattern

facts.note: Task text mentioning HTTP/REST exposure of wagon artifacts.

values: artifact-to-REST endpoint mapping specified or changed
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that extracts artifact-name -> endpoint/verb pairs from any changed file (plans, acceptances, docs, contracts, code).
Whether an artifact is exposed for external consumption over HTTP can only be judged from context.

fires: An artifact-to-REST mapping is written for `match:result` so external consumers can read it over HTTP.
An acceptance or contract asserts the HTTP method/path for `session:new` or `session:closed`.
A category facet artifact (e.g. `ux:foundations.colors`) gets an externally consumed endpoint.
doesNotFire: An artifact that is only consumed internally and never exposed over HTTP.
Handler internals change without any artifact-to-endpoint mapping being specified or changed.
Edits that touch no artifact names or endpoints.

given: An artifact named `{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]` is exposed to external consumers over a REST API
when: its artifact-to-REST endpoint mapping is specified or changed
then: Map the artifact name to an endpoint following `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]`, with category facets adding path segments.
prefer: Turn each category facet into an extra path segment (`ux:foundations` → `GET /uxs/{id}/foundations`; `ux:foundations.colors` → `GET /uxs/{id}/foundations/colors`; `match:result` → `GET /matches/{id}/result`).
Follow the source's shorter forms where they apply: `session:new` → `POST /sessions` (collection, no `{id}` or resource segment); `player:identity` → `GET /players/{id}` (no resource segment).

Select the HTTP verb from the resource keyword (creation→POST, read→GET, mutation→PUT, removal→DELETE): POST new/created/registered/started; GET result/active/config/events/foundations; PUT updated/closed/completed; DELETE terminated/deleted.
avoid: Hand-crafting paths that drop the plural domain or the category segments, or otherwise diverge from the pattern beyond the source's own `session:new` and `player:identity` forms.
Choosing a verb that contradicts the resource keyword, e.g. mapping `session:closed` to POST (closed → PUT, not POST).
why: A deterministic artifact-to-REST mapping lets external consumers address wagon artifacts over HTTP, and choosing the verb from the resource keyword keeps the API surface consistent with the artifact's lifecycle semantics.
evidence: Every externally exposed artifact has an endpoint matching `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]` (or one of the source's example forms), with category facets as path segments.
Each declared HTTP verb matches the resource keyword table (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE).

Source examples hold: `ux:foundations` -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations; `ux:foundations.colors` -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations/colors; `match:result` -> GET /matches/{id}/result; `session:new` -> POST /sessions; `player:identity` -> GET /players/{id}.
verifier_detail: Term endpoint_pattern (label 'REST endpoint pattern'): pattern `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]`; artifact names map to REST API endpoints for external consumption; category facets add path segments.

Term verb_mapping (label 'Resource-keyword to HTTP verb table'): the resource keyword selects the HTTP method; creation keywords → POST, read → GET, mutation → PUT, removal → DELETE. POST: [new, created, registered, started]; GET: [result, active, config, events, foundations]; PUT: [updated, closed, completed]; DELETE: [terminated, deleted].

Positive endpoint examples: `ux:foundations -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations`; `ux:foundations.colors -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations/colors`; `match:result -> GET /matches/{id}/result`; `session:new -> POST /sessions`; `player:identity -> GET /players/{id}`.

Source examples deviate from the literal pattern: `session:new` targets the collection `/sessions` (no `{id}`/resource segment); `player:identity` maps to `/players/{id}` (no resource segment). Do not flag these. The source does not state whether every creation keyword targets the collection; do not generalize beyond the examples. Domain pluralization is English-style (`match`→`matches`).

Verb examples: positive `session:new -> POST /sessions  # new -> POST`, `match:result -> GET /matches/{id}/result  # result -> GET`; negative `session:closed mapped to POST  # closed -> PUT, not POST`.
No automated implementation exists (implementation.type: none); compliance is reviewer/LLM-judged.
